title: Remove a staple without tearing the papers
instruction: Remove the staple without tearing either sheet.
context: Preparing documents for scanning requires releasing a clinched fastener while preserving thin paper around its holes.
setup: Proposed fixed setup: two white 80 gsm paper sheets, each 210 × 148 × 0.1 mm, on a 210 × 128 × 20 mm document support with a 1.5 × 16 × 8 mm clinch-clearance pocket. In station coordinates, sheet centres are (0.32, 0) and (0.32, 0.012) m, at heights 767.55 and 767.67 mm. A steel staple has a 12.8 mm crown, 6 mm legs and 0.50 × 0.30 mm wire section, clinched through both sheets at x=0.227, y=−0.050 m, through existing 0.8 × 0.6 mm holes. A 108 × 18 × 16 mm steel/ABS forked lever remover rests at x=0.28, y=−0.20 m. The table is 747.5 mm high. All simulation coordinates receive one fixed origin shift before construction, preserving relative geometry. No paper pins or fixed staple. Complete robot extraction and final setup evidence remain unvalidated.
scoring: 0.5 when at least one whole staple leg is clear of both sheets and the preservation checks pass. 1.0 when both legs are clear, the intact staple is at least 10 mm from either sheet, and staple and papers remain released for three seconds. A new tear over 2 mm beyond an original hole, any new cut or puncture elsewhere, a broken staple, altered sheets or invalid evidence gives zero. Creases alone are not tears. The staple may remain in or on a remover that the robot has released onto the work surface.
run_limit: Proposed 600 control steps (30 seconds at 20 Hz). The 386-action extraction-and-release plan still requires a valid native demonstration.
reset_notes: Use fresh matched paper and one fresh staple for every trial. Record both sides before and after. Reuse the remover only while intact.
fidelity: Each sheet is a flexible assembly of 0.1 mm native box panels with passive bending hinges and finite breaking strength. This approximates inextensible isotropic paper; elastic bending does not retain creases. Explicit punctures and plastic steel bending preserve the removal mechanism. Every physics step checks paper continuity, steel integrity and wire crossings. Loaded extraction remains unverified.
